items.title: Generative AI on This Crown's Cover
items.excerpt: Ilona Andrews says the cover of 'This Crown Will Not Rule Me' contained generative-AI elements despite no-AI clauses in both the authors' and Tor's contracts; Tor says the AI use happened without its or the authors' knowledge and is commissioning a replacement cover and tightening art review. Off-list primary source (no on-list coverage found).

items.title: COPYRIGHT NEWS—Anthropic and Meta self-helped themselves to AI training materials, new lawsuit asserts
items.excerpt: Carlson LLC, copyright owner of Richard Carlson's 'Don't Sweat the Small Stuff' series, sued Anthropic and Meta in N.D. Cal. (3:26-cv-14248, filed Nov 19), alleging more than two dozen self-help books were taken from Books3/Anna's Archive and scanned to train AI models; Carlson opted out of the Bartz settlement. New case, not the Bartz payouts thread.

history_match.title: Stanford professors opt out of Anthropic settlement and file their own lawsuit over pirated books used to train Claude

items.title: Caine Prize Clears Zimbabwean Winner of AI Allegations After Forensic Review
items.excerpt: The Caine Prize confirmed Simbarashe Kundizeza as 2026 winner after a 'human-centred' investigation, including cyber-forensic metadata analysis of his drafts, found no evidence that The Blue Fighter was AI-written, overriding a Pangram 100%-AI flag cited by The Atlantic. Reports say the prize also added new rules; a formal prize decision rather than another detector story.

history_match.title: Caine Prize for African writing finds 'no evidence' winning story was AI generated

items.title: Author Says the Hundreds of Full-Length Romance Novels She Publishes Every Year Are Very High Quality in Spite of AI Usage
items.excerpt: South African romance writer Coral Hart says she has published hundreds of AI-assisted novels (about 370 since February 2025, under 10+ pen names), drafting whole books in one pass across multiple LLMs, and insists the quality holds up.

items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
items.excerpt: Guardian interactive feature on AI across publishing: an indie author producing hundreds of AI books a year, literary agents with no reliable process for AI submissions, and the industry's scramble to set rules.

items.title: New Jersey Mom Accuses Publisher of Using AI To Give 10-Year-Old Daughter's Drawing a Boob Job
items.excerpt: A viral TikTok (329K views) alleges that student-book publisher Studenttreasures used AI to alter a 10-year-old's illustrations, cover included, for her school-project book, including sexualising a character. Off-list source; children's-book AI illustration angle, unverified allegation.

items.title: Australian Society of Authors, Australian Publishers Association among orgs launching 'Not AI's to Take' campaign
items.excerpt: The ASA, APA and media and creative bodies launched the 'Not AI's to Take' petition urging Canberra to keep copyright protections and require permission before AI firms train on Australian creative work; reports say music has since won a carve-out. Publish time from URL date plus feed timestamp (no meta tag).

items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Analysis of the Third Circuit's ROSS opinion for publishers: the more an AI product is marketed as solving research tasks, the less transformative its training use looks, which strengthens publishers' licensing leverage. The ROSS decision itself was covered 10-06; this is the publisher-facing analysis.

items.title: The Anatomy of 'Harm': An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO on the organisation's study quantifying how generative AI harms publishers and authors, and what collective licensing can do about it.

history_match.title: IFRRO Releases New Study on AI, Copyright Issues

items.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
items.excerpt: ALTA and 11 other writer groups filed a brief backing the Authors Guild's suit against OpenAI and Microsoft, arguing AI translation could turn translators 'from interpreters into primarily editors of large language model outputs' and that literary translations are copyrighted works. Note: part of the In re OpenAI amicus thread (deprioritized unless there is a ruling). Date from body byline (Nov 18, 2026).

history_match.title: Publishers urge US court to reject OpenAI's fair use defence in copyright case

items.title: News Summary: Audible Launches Audio Discovery Trailers; Guardian Calls AI Literary Wild West
items.excerpt: Audible's new 'audio discovery' gives listeners enhanced trailers: highlight clips plus synopsis and character insights narrated by Audible's AI virtual voice. May overlap the 11-17 Audible AI previews card.

items.title: AI is giving writers the support publishing cannot
items.excerpt: Comment piece by Marian Stan arguing AI can give aspiring novelists the editorial feedback they have long struggled to get from publishing. Opinion piece, behind a paywall.

items.title: Publishing Ireland conference: AI and rising costs high on the agenda
items.excerpt: Publishing Ireland's autumn conference covered AI and the cost pressures on the book trade. Paywalled; AI depth unverified.

items.title: Celebrity ghostwriters are now selling points, not secrets. Is AI a factor?
items.excerpt: Ghostwriters behind celebrity memoirs are increasingly credited on the cover; the piece asks whether naming a human writer has become a marker of authenticity in the AI era. Off-list analysis; date only (20261117).

items.title: Namoo - 부모님의 이야기를 AI 인터뷰로 기록해 이북과 오디오북으로 만들어 주는 앱
items.excerpt: Namoo, a Korean indie app launch, runs AI interviews with parents about their lives and turns the transcripts into a memoir ebook and audiobook, a consumer take on AI ghostwriting. Off-list; small launch.

items.title: AI could bring books to radio, but broadcasters still need to direct the story
items.excerpt: Synthetic voices could let radio stations test serialised literary readings and narrated essays, but success will depend on editorial judgement, rights clearance and listener trust. Off-list; analysis.
